title: "Sales Teams: Send a Narrated Pitch Deck, Not a Cold PDF" (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Send a Narrated Pitch Deck, Not a PDF
slides.notes: The prospect asked for something to share with the team. You sent a PDF. Here's why a narrated video pitch deck makes the case when you're not there.

slides.title: A PDF strips out your reasoning
bullets: The champion has to retell it
slides.notes: Sales slides are built to be presented. Without your voice, readers jump to pricing, your champion retells it from memory, and every slide gets the same weight.

slides.title: Situation, problem, answer, proof, next step
bullets: The answer: one slide, not five
slides.notes: Keep it short and specific to the buyer. This pattern works because it mirrors how a buyer thinks about a purchase.

slides.title: Headlines and notes carry the pitch
bullets: After: "Your team gets one place to track every renewal"
slides.notes: Headlines should tell the story with the sound off. Write speaker notes the way you'd say them: short sentences, plain words. If you trip, the narrator will too.

slides.title: Send it so it gets watched
slides.notes: Many people watch forwarded videos with the sound off, so turn on captions. Then send a brief email that states the length and the ask.

slides.title: Ordinary slides in, extraordinary pitch out
slides.notes: On Pro, a.i. directs your pitch, tightening the story and timing each scene to the narration. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
